title: sync and context
subtitle: Mutexes, WaitGroups, cancellation
focus_note: A context is canceled when its parent is, when its own cancel func is called, or when its deadline passes. Every WithCancel, WithTimeout and WithDeadline returns a cancel func you must call.

drills.prompt: Which sync type waits for a group of goroutines to finish?

drills.hint: so Unlock runs on every return path

drills.prompt: Can the same goroutine lock a sync.Mutex twice?
drills.note: Go's mutexes are not reentrant: the second Lock deadlocks.

drills.prompt: What is the zero value of a sync.Mutex?
drills.note: No constructor needed: declare it and use it.

drills.prompt: Which sync type runs a function exactly once, even with concurrent callers?
Which context function cancels after a duration?
drills.note: context.WithDeadline takes an absolute time instead.

drills.prompt: Which channel does a context close when it's canceled?
drills.note: After Done is closed, ctx.Err() says why: context.Canceled or context.DeadlineExceeded.

drills.prompt: Which go command flag finds data races at run time?
Why must you call the cancel func from context.WithCancel even when the work finished?
answers: Until it's called (or the parent is canceled), the context and its resources stay alive: a leak. go vet's lostcancel check warns about it.

drills.prompt: Why is copying a sync.Mutex after first use a bug?
answers: The copy carries the original's lock state and is a separate lock, so the two no longer guard the same data. go vet's copylocks check flags it.
